title: Why Tibo won't raise VC again: user validation beats investor validation
summary: Tibo explains why he, having raised VC before, now bootstraps: investor money creates fake validation, VC power-law math pushes you toward lottery-ticket growth instead of a free profitable business, and most internet companies only need paying users. He reports $1M MRR across 5 bootstrapped, profitable products.

principles.text: Investor money is not market validation; only paying customers validate a product.
principles.quote: VC money is not user validation. It never was. The only validation that matters is someone opening their wallet and paying for your product.

principles.text: Raising is the start of the work, not an achievement worth celebrating.
principles.quote: Congratulating a founder on raising is like congratulating a chef on getting the vegetables.

principles.text: VCs optimise for a 100x lottery ticket, not your sustainable profitable business, so decent growth can lose their support.
principles.quote: They expect 9/10 of their bets to fail. They need just one company per fund to return everything.

principles.text: VC pressure shifts you from building for users to chasing the next round, costing freedom.
principles.quote: You stop building for users and start working just to raise the next round.

principles.text: Bootstrapped, cash-generating products remove exit pressure and give freedom to move fast or slow.
principles.quote: When you bootstrap, and your products print cash, there's no pressure to exit.

principles.text: Raise only when scale precedes revenue (infrastructure) or compliance costs are huge; otherwise get paying users.
principles.quote: But most internet businesses don't need it. You need users who pay. That's the only math that matters.
